one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban delivers the second of a three-column series on PNoy's Sona-cited daang matuwid achievements -- focusing on the PDAF (Priority Development Assistance Fund) cases against Senators Jinggoy Estrada, Bong Revilla, and Juan Ponce Enrile. After DOJ preliminary investigation and OOO probable-cause findings, separate Informations were filed and raffled to three different Sandiganbayan divisions: the First Division for Revilla, the Third for Enrile, the Fifth for Estrada. When charged with capital offenses, accused usually launch three major battles to win their freedom: (1) an initial battle to stop the court from issuing warrants of arrest and detention on the ground that the Information and supporting documents do not show 'probable cause'; (2) an ensuing fight for bail on the ground that the prosecution's evidence is not 'strong'; and (3) a final battle for acquittal on the ground that evidence failed to prove guilt 'beyond reasonable doubt.' Interlocutory orders along the way are often challenged via certiorari petitions in the SC. Estrada: the Fifth Division found probable cause; the SC upheld it; the SBN is now conducting bail hearings every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. Three certiorari petitions are pending -- two by Estrada (to exclude alleged AMLC-reported bank transactions, and to suppress Benhur Luy's cash/check reports and testimony) and one by the OOO (contesting the SBN's refusal to transfer Estrada from the PNP Custodial Center to Camp Bagong Diwa in Taguig). Revilla: probable-cause certiorari dismissed by the SC; SBN fully heard and denied bail Dec 1, 2014; MR denied March 26, 2015; pretrial set Sept 30 -- proceedings in a more advanced stage than Estrada's. Three SC petitions pending: two by Revilla (probable cause and bail denial) and one by the OOO (transfer to Camp Bagong Diwa). Enrile, taking a more proactive stance via counsels Estelito Mendoza and Eleazar Reyes, is challenging the usual procedure with two SC certiorari petitions. First: the Information for plunder filed by the OOO is invalid because it did not allege enough specific facts to enable him to prepare his defense (bill of particulars). Second: the Constitution guarantees bail to the accused at all times -- the only exception being when (1) the evidence of guilt is strong AND (2) the penalty prescribed is reclusion perpetua or life imprisonment. Until the prosecution proves its evidence is 'strong,' the accused cannot be detained; the present procedure of immediately detaining accused prior to that ruling is illogical and unconstitutional. He further argues that even if convicted, reclusion perpetua cannot be imposed because he should be credited with two mitigating circumstances: old age (over 70 years) and voluntary surrender. The SC will resolve these petitions soon; should Enrile win any of them, he may be freed from detention. In sum, given that trial on the merits has not even begun for any of the three senators, these plunder and graft cases cannot be decided during PNoy's term, which ends on June 30, 2016.
